title: Compare what logrotate is configured to rotate against what actually exists
explanation: `cat /etc/logrotate.d/billing` shows the config targets `/var/log/billing/app.log`, but `ls /var/log/billing/` shows the real, ever-growing file is `billing.log` — a rename that never made it into the logrotate config.

title: Explain why a wrong path produces zero visible errors
explanation: `missingok` in the config explicitly tells logrotate it's fine if the configured path doesn't exist — so instead of erroring or warning, logrotate just runs on schedule and matches nothing, forever, with nothing to alert anyone that rotation stopped happening.

title: Fix the path to match the real, current file
explanation: `sudo sed -i 's#/var/log/billing/app.log#/var/log/billing/billing.log#' /etc/logrotate.d/billing` points the config at the file that actually exists and is actually growing.

title: Verify by forcing a run rather than waiting on the schedule
explanation: `sudo logrotate --force /etc/logrotate.d/billing` triggers rotation immediately; `ls /var/log/billing/` should now show `billing.log.1`, and `billing.log` itself is back to empty — since this config uses `copytruncate`, the original is copied out then truncated in place rather than renamed.

title: Recognize the general pattern for next time
explanation: Whenever an app's log file gets renamed or moved, its logrotate config is exactly the kind of dependent config that's easy to forget — and with `missingok` in play, there's no built-in signal that it's silently doing nothing; only comparing the config against reality catches it.
